label: Mid-prefix (steps 4-5) after m/i/o/x, strongest for ..f.m prefixes
explanation: Fires only on original-phase inputs at steps 3-6 (96% of mass at steps 3-5; peak at step 4). It never fires at steps 0-2, at step 7 or later, or in the copy phase; a small amount (1.6%) shows up on <DEL> when L=4. Inside that window it fires on only a few percent of steps, and which steps depends on the earlier tokens. The previous input being m carries 57% of mass (15x lift); i, o and x add a little more. The strongest activations (~0.9-1.0 of max) are at step 4 right after a prefix like _ f f m, _ f s m or _ p f m, i.e. m at position 3 with f at position 1 or 2. Activation then drops off over steps 5-6. The m step itself barely activates. Neither the window alone (precision 3%) nor the token conditions alone capture it. The predicate catches about 58% of mass at ~19% precision; t==4 & prev_tok==m alone gives 57% precision but only 29% of mass. Lower-activation firings are spread across many prefixes without an obvious single rule.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=m (+5.50), orig1=f (+4.44), orig2=f (+3.63), t=4 (+3.49), t=5 (+3.33), orig0=2 (+2.77). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-6.52), t=8 (-5.19), orig0=m (-5.03), phase=2 (-4.94).
